content: {"summary":"Intermittent catalog‑api‑02 database connection failures began at 20:25 UTC on 19 Sep 2025 because a zone‑file push to internal‑dns‑02 omitted the database host record, causing that DNS server to return NXDOMAIN for queries that were randomly routed to it.","likely_cause":"Missing database DNS record after a zone‑file push to internal‑dns‑02","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"A zone‑file push was applied to internal‑dns‑02 at 20:25 on 19 Sep 2025","evidence_ids":["INC-0081#2","INC-0081#0"],"quote":"The push that landed at 20:25 fitted the start of the errors."},{"text":"The push omitted the database DNS record, causing internal‑dns‑02 to answer NXDOMAIN for the DB name","evidence_ids":["INC-0081#1","INC-0081#0"],"quote":"A window opened by a query to internal-dns-02 carried `NXDOMAIN` for up to half a minute."},{"text":"Random forwarding between two DNS servers caused intermittent successes and failures","evidence_ids":["INC-0081#1"],"quote":"Pods ask the cluster CoreDNS, which forwards `prod.internal` queries to one internal-dns server picked at random"}],"next_checks":["Inspect the zone file version deployed to internal-dns-02 at 20:25 to confirm the missing record","Compare SOA serials of internal-dns-01 and internal-dns-02 for the prod.internal zone","Check CoreDNS cache entries for the database hostname during the incident window","Review runbook RB-020 steps that were applied to resolve the DNS disagreement"]}
